title: Apple Cinnamon Baked Oatmeal
subtitle: Warm spiced oat squares with tender apple chunks for easy portioning.
description: Warm oat squares with apple and cinnamon — portioned from a 9x13 so ten firefighters get the same bowl without standing over a pot. Holds in a low oven between eaters.

ingredients.name: Chopped Walnuts
ingredients.notes: and butter pats at the line

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a 9x13 baking dish. Toss diced apples with half the cinnamon and spread in the bottom of the dish.

steps.title: Mix the oat base
steps.instruction: Whisk oats, milk, eggs, brown sugar, remaining cinnamon, nutmeg, and a pinch of salt until combined. The mixture should look like thick pourable batter.

steps.title: Pour and top
steps.instruction: Pour oat mixture over apples and scatter walnuts on top. Tap the dish to settle the batter evenly for uniform slices.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Bake until the center is set, edges are golden, and a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean. The top should spring back lightly when pressed.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares. Serve warm with maple syrup and optional butter pats. Hold uncovered at 200°F for up to 30 minutes.

stationWorkflow: Dice apples and mix batter while the oven preheats—this bake is forgiving on timing.
Cut squares in the pan with a sharp knife wiped between cuts for clean portions.
Set maple and walnuts at the line so customization doesn't bottleneck the hot squares.
cleanupNotes: Soak the 9x13 in warm water immediately—baked oatmeal cement is easier to release when warm.
Line the prep bowl with a thin film of oil before mixing sticky oat batter for faster cleanup.
leftovers: Wrap squares individually and reheat at 325°F for 10 minutes with a splash of milk on top.
Crumble cold squares into a skillet with butter and pan-fry until crisp for oatmeal hash browns.
